source_text: ταῖς τῶν ὑπὸ χεῖρα καὶ ἐξουσίαν εὐχαῖς, τὴν τῆς δυσσεβείας ἐπιφέρει γραφὴν, εἰ μὴ πληροῦν ἕλοιντο τὰ ἐπηγγελμένα. Ἀποφάσκουσι δὲ καὶ τὸ ἀνεῖσθαι δεῖν ἁμαρτιῶν ἀπονέμει· προαιρέσεως γὰρ, καὶ οὐκ ἀνάγκης καρποὶ τὰ εἰς Θεὸν ἀναθήματα.
pass_a_gloss: [Continuation of §27: for to the masters, father and husband, having agreed and as it were nodded assent] to the vows of those under hand and authority, he brings upon [them] the indictment of impiety, if they should not choose to fulfill the things announced/promised. And to those refusing he assigns also that there must be release from sins; for the dedications toward God [are] fruits of free choice, and not of compulsion.
pass_a_gloss_with_greek: [Continuation of §27: for to the masters, father and husband, having agreed and as it were nodded assent] to the vows (εὐχή) of those under hand (χείρ) and authority (ἐξουσία), he brings upon [them] (ἐπιφέρω) the indictment (γραφή) of impiety (δυσσέβεια), if they should not choose (αἱρέομαι) to fulfill (πληρόω) the things announced/promised (ἐπαγγέλλομαι). And to those refusing (ἀποφάσκω) he assigns (ἀπονέμω) also that there must (δεῖ) be release (ἀνίημι, pass.) from sins (ἁμαρτία); for the dedications (ἀνάθημα) toward God [are] fruits (καρπός) of free choice (προαίρεσις), and not of compulsion (ἀνάγκη).
pass_b_english: Cyril: …to the vows of those under their hand and authority, he brings the charge of impiety if they do not choose to fulfill what was promised (Numbers 30:14–15). But when they refuse, he also rules that there must be release from sin; for offerings dedicated to God are the fruits of free choice, not of compulsion.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; a column may cut mid-sentence or mid-word.

Completes the sentence begun at the end of §27 (dative 'τοῖς κυρίοις ... συνθεμένοις' governed by 'ἐπιφέρει γραφήν'), so the section opens 'Cyril: …'; rendered 'against the masters ... he brings the charge'. Numbers 30:14–15 (English; LXX 30:15–16): a husband who stays silent confirms the vows, and if he cancels them later he 'shall bear her iniquity'; cited as the provision Cyril summarizes. Ambiguity: 'Ἀποφάσκουσι δὲ καὶ τὸ ἀνεῖσθαι δεῖν ἁμαρτιῶν ἀπονέμει' – the dative plural points to the father or husband who refuses, but the release may be the woman's (compare 'the Lord will cleanse her', Numbers 30:5, 8, 12); English keeps it impersonal ('there must be release from sin'). 'Fruits of free choice, not of compulsion' may echo 2 Corinthians 9:7 or Philemon 1:14 but quotes neither; left uncited. This short section ends Book 16.
